answer: Price capacity, not headcount. Each epoch consensus auctions S answer slots, bids escrowed in a vault and burned on failed grading, price floor f ≥ R/S (R = fixed epoch pool); each slot pays at most R/S. A cluster winning k slots with k identities pays k·f ≥ k·R/S: every extra identity buys at least the reward it can win, no cheaper. Identities are mere pigment; the floor is the load-bearing timber — drop f below R/S and empty epochs let clones capture the pool. Assumes consensus enforces escrow and cap; deters profit, not influence.
